reason: Start the glucose and amino acid route by bringing glucose across the villus.
expectation: Glucose will enter the villus, probably reaching its blood vessels; the route toward the liver may need another step.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also a goal, but I will start with the blood-bound nutrients.

effect: Glucose has crossed into a villus capillary; its onward route to the liver remains to be shown.
reaction: The result matches my expectation, though it does not explain how glucose crosses the cell.
reason: Follow the other blood-bound nutrient across the villus.
expectation: Amino acids will cross intestinal cells into villus blood, with a later step possibly showing their route to the liver.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption is also needed, but finishing the paired nutrient routes first seems efficient.

effect: Both glucose and amino acids have entered villus blood; I can now combine their routes.
reaction: The parallel result is clear but again leaves the crossing mechanism unexplained.
reason: Combine the two blood-borne nutrients to advance their route toward the liver.
expectation: Their routes will be grouped for transport toward the liver, though a separate vessel may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: Fat absorption also needs attention, but I want to finish the paired blood route first.

effect: Glucose and amino acids now travel in portal blood toward the liver, completing that goal.
reaction: The shared route is clear, though combining the nutrients felt more like grouping than a physical step.
reason: Begin the remaining fat-absorption route at the villus.
expectation: Fat digestion products will enter intestinal cells, where they may need packaging before reaching lymph.

alternatives.reason: Packaging will likely be needed, but I want to follow the fat products into the villus first.

effect: Fatty acids and monoglycerides are inside the intestinal cells, ready for the offered packaging step.
reaction: The result matches my expectation, though it does not explain how the products entered the cells.
reason: Package the absorbed fat for its route into lymph.
expectation: The cell will use the lipid and protein materials to package the fat into lipoprotein particles; entry into the lacteal may require another step.

alternatives.reason: The lacteal is needed for lymph entry, but packaging the fat first seems natural.

effect: The intestinal cells rebuild and package fat into chylomicrons, ready for the lacteal route.
reaction: The explanation makes the packaging step clear and introduces chylomicrons by name.
reason: Use the lacteal entrance to send the packaged fat into lymph.
expectation: Chylomicrons will leave the intestinal cells and enter the villus lymph vessel, completing the fat route.

effect: Chylomicrons enter the villus lymph vessel and travel onward to blood, completing the fat route.
reaction: The final explanation usefully connects lymph back to blood.

mostWorthwhile.text: Packaging fat and sending it into lymph was the most worthwhile passage: it explains why fat follows a different initial route from glucose and amino acids.

leastWorthwhile.text: The parallel glucose and amino-acid crossings were clear but repetitive, and neither explained how the molecules cross the intestinal cells.

surprise.text: Intestinal cells rebuild fat before packaging it into chylomicrons, which enter lymph before reaching blood.

arbitrary.text: Combining glucose and amino acids felt like grouping two routes rather than a physical process, although the resulting portal-blood route had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue to see how absorbed nutrients are handled after reaching blood and the liver, though I would hope for more explanation of transport mechanisms.
